name: Retinal Fundus
desc: The back of the eye through a fundus camera: a warm choroidal orange field, the bright optic disc off to the nasal side with its cupped centre, and the retinal vasculature streaming out of it — superior and inferior arcades sweeping around the dark avascular macula, arteries thin and bright with a central light reflex, veins broader and darker — blood pulsing along every vessel on the cardiac cycle while the camera illumination pool drifts across the retina, shown as a fundus photo, a fluorescein angiogram, a red-free monochrome, or a schematic vessel map.

energy.doc: illumination strength — brightness of the fundus and its light pool

scale.doc: magnification into the fundus (zoom the field of view)

density.doc: how much of the vessel tree is grown out

pulse.doc: amplitude of the arterial pulse travelling the vessels

drift.doc: speed of the drifting camera illumination pool

hue.doc: choroidal warmth of the photo look

x.doc: pan across the retina when magnified

y.doc: pan up/down the retina when magnified

style.doc: colour fundus photo / bright fluorescein angiogram / red-free green monochrome / blueprint vessel map

seed.doc: deterministic vessel tree, choroid mottle, and eye orientation
